_comment: EXT-63 SMOKE, arm 22 — arm 20 (canonical + LV-1 + LV-2 + LV-4) + CARD LV-5, the
WITHIN-EPOCH mu (docs/SPEC_level_information_budget.md S12).  Single knob vs arm 20:
network.rx_cb_carry_demean_within.
WHAT LV-5 REMOVES.  LV-2 reduced mu at the SERIAL POST-SOLVE harvest and applied it
to the NEXT epoch's folds.  That is a feedback delay, and its loop gain scales with
how much carry information folds: harmless while the defective frame screen withheld
two thirds of the priors (arm 19: 51.9 % folded, settled sd 4.98 TECU), a ~3-epoch
LIMIT CYCLE once LV-4 admits them all (arm 21: 97.5 % folded, settled sd 15.53,
The lag was never necessary.  Both terms of the carry innovation -- the stashed
ABSOLUTE posterior and the FROZEN x_lin(cb) -- are known before PASS B, so mu is now
reduced SERIALLY between PASS A and PASS B over the stations present THIS epoch, and
PASS B folds against it.  Same race contract (one serial writer, parallel readers).
PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RUN:
- The limit cycle DAMPS.  a00 over 20 ep should look like arm 18/20's envelope
without the epoch-to-epoch alternation; the real test is the 1 h settled sd
(arm 23), so treat this smoke as wiring + counters.
- Fold fraction unchanged from arm 20 (~94 %): LV-5 changes WHEN mu is computed,
not which rows fold.  A materially different fold count means the prepass
candidate set disagrees with PASS B's folded set by more than the expected
column-dropout margin -- investigate before reading the level.
- The run-end LV-5 line reports the RESIDUAL: the folded set's own raw common mode
MINUS the mu applied to it.  Predict mean |resid| well below max |mu| (order 10 %
or less).  A residual the size of mu means the correction is decorative -- the
candidate set and the folded set would then be effectively different populations,
and the honest fix is a two-pass PASS B, not a bigger mu.
- max |mu| should FALL back toward arm 18's ~2 m: with no lag, mu no longer chases
its own tail.
